newsitem.title: LEBANON: Most leading shares up on Beirut bourse.
newsitem.headline: Most leading shares up on Beirut bourse.

text.p: Most leading shares rose on the Beirut Stock Exchange and brokers said the lifting of a U.S. travel ban on Lebanon boosted Solidere shares on Thursday.
Both Solidere A and B shares rose 1.9 percent each to $13.125 and $13.25 repectively from $12.875 and $13 a day earlier.

"It is a temporary psychological effect of the decision to lift the U.S. travel ban. Solidere shares will be consolidating at their current levels. It is healthy for the shares," a broker who requested anonymity told Reuters.

The United States lifted on Wednesday a 10-year-old travel ban on U.S. citizens visiting Lebanon. Solidere, Lebanon's biggest company, is leading a multi-billion dollar reconstruction drive in Beirut.
Bank of Beirut shares continued surging, touching a new record high at $5.75 from $5.5. This marked a 164 percent rise in the share price since it was issued earlier this year.
Brokers had expected the share to reach $6 next week.
Banque Audi shares rose to $28 from $27.875. "I think Audi will move up on earnings forecast for the second half of the year," the broker said.
Banque Libanaise pour le Commerce fell 2.3 percent to $21.75 from $22.25 when it was last traded on Tuesday.
The LIBX bank index rose 0.88 percent to 197.71. The BLOM general index rose 1.61 percent to 1124.45 and the LISPI climbed 0.59 percent to 97.30.
BSE turnover climbed to 327,033 shares from 298,430 for a value of $4,004,592 against $3,490,593.
There was no trade in the four listed industrial firms -- Uniceramic, Ciments Blanc, Ciments Libanais and Eternit.
